title: List All Triggers
description: Learn how to list all triggers in a SQL Server database by querying sys.triggers.

data.text: To list all triggers in a SQL Server database, query the sys.triggers system view.

data.title: List all triggers using sys.triggers
data.content: Returns trigger names and whether they are INSTEAD OF triggers.
data.code:
SELECT
    name,
    is_instead_of_trigger
FROM
    sys.triggers
WHERE
    type = 'TR';

data.text: Join to the Parent Table and List Events

`sys.triggers` only stores the trigger itself. To show which table a trigger belongs to, join `parent_id` to `sys.objects`. For DML triggers, `sys.trigger_events` tells you whether it fires on INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, or a combination.

data.title: List triggers with their table and events
data.content: Aggregates the firing events into a comma-separated list and shows the parent table name.
data.code:
SELECT
    t.name                                   AS trigger_name,
    OBJECT_SCHEMA_NAME(t.parent_id)          AS schema_name,
    OBJECT_NAME(t.parent_id)                 AS table_name,
    t.is_instead_of_trigger,
    t.is_disabled,
    STRING_AGG(te.type_desc, ', ')           AS events
FROM sys.triggers AS t
JOIN sys.trigger_events AS te
    ON te.object_id = t.object_id
WHERE t.type = 'TR'
  AND t.parent_class = 1        -- object-level (DML) triggers
GROUP BY
    t.name,
    t.parent_id,
    t.is_instead_of_trigger,
    t.is_disabled
ORDER BY schema_name, table_name, trigger_name;

data.title: Database-level triggers are different
data.text: DDL triggers live at the database or server scope, so their `parent_class` is 0 and they have no parent table. Use `sys.server_triggers` for server-scoped logon triggers. If you only query `sys.triggers` with no filter you will mix DML and database DDL triggers together.

data.title: List Triggers Key Points
points: Use sys.triggers to list all triggers in the database.
The is_instead_of_trigger column indicates if a trigger is an INSTEAD OF trigger.
Filter by type = 'TR' to return only triggers (not other objects).
You can also use sys.objects with type = 'TR' as an alternative.
